reasoning: Spot 4WF-4-WAY-3--061: facing_bet=0, hero MP is the preflop 3-bettor, AcJd on Qc9h3s, 4-way 3-bet pot, OOP. Bucket: 4-way-3-bet-pot-OOP-cbet-missed-board. Per-villain range chains. UTG opened 2.5bb then called a 3-bet: range-capped (no AA/KK/AK which 4-bet or fold; continues with QQ-88, KQ-suited, AQs, suited connectors, some AJo). On Q-9-3 UTG has connected range: Q-x value (QK, QJ), sets (99, 33, QQ), over-pair JJ-TT partial. CO cold-called the 3-bet OOP: range very strong (JJ-99, AQs, KQs, suited broadways) — no AA/KK/AK (would 4-bet), no weak hands (cold-call of 3-bet is premium). CO connects with QQ (set), 99, JJ. SB cold-called the 3-bet from SB: similar premium-capped range (JJ-99, AQs, KJs, suited connectors), no 4-bet combos. SB has set potential on 9-3. Hero's AcJd: complete air on Qc9h3s — two overcards (A beats Q, but J is below Q); backdoor club FD (Ac). Equity realization: 4-way pot, realization factor ~0.75 vs three independent ranges. Hero is OOP, acts first among all players; all 3 villains can apply pressure behind. AcJd has ~25% raw equity vs combined 4-way continuing ranges — but realization is suppressed. Spot-specific factors: hero as 3-bettor has range advantage (range includes QQ/AK/AA more than villains' capped ranges), which justifies a small c-bet frequency even on missed boards. OOP-early position means all 3 apply pressure; donk-lead frequency should be calibrated toward small c-bet to maintain range credibility and deny free cards to drawing hands (FDs in clubs/diamonds, 87-suited gutshots). A 25% small c-bet leverages the 3-bettor's polar range image; checks too often cede the pot to UTG's connected range and allow Q-x hands free SDV. Decision: BET 25%. This is a mixed-strategy spot — hero's range includes QQ+/AK that also bet small here, so AJ rides the 3-bettor's polarized small c-bet frequency for fold equity against villain air. Alternative CHECK gives up initiative vs UTG-connected Q-x hands and cedes fold equity entirely; UTG's capped range bets Q-x for value, putting hero in a difficult check-call-fold situation OOP on later streets.

Now CO has checked river, which weakens CO's range toward realized-equity marginal hands: two-pair (J-8, J-5, J-3), single pair 9-x, busted FD (hearts, clubs). Equity realization: river is HU, factor ≈1.0. Hero's JsTs on Js4d3s8c5h: the spade flush did not complete (board has 3 spades but the secondary_axis label is 'missed-FD-value-bet'; hero's remaining value is top pair Jacks with T kicker, no flush made). Spot-specific factors: CO checked river after two streets of aggression — this is the critical tell that CO's range collapsed toward marginal SDV hands. Hero's J-T is top pair with mediocre kicker vs CO's checked range. The missed-FD axis means hero's hand lost its draw dimension; remaining value is thin-top-pair. Against CO's busted-FD + marginal-pair checking range, a small 33% river value bet extracts from worse hands (9-x, 8-x, 5-x pairs) that will call once but would not lead themselves. Decision: BET 33% for thin value. CHECK surrenders value against CO's calling-range hands that would call one bet but never lead. The risk is CO snap-calls with J-x two-pair (J-8, J-5) or slow-played set — but those combos are thin vs CO's overall checked range composition on this runout.

Spot 4WF-MW-AXIS-466: facing_bet=0, hero SB, AsJd on 8s5s2c, 4-way SRP, OOP (SB), first to act among three villains. Bucket: MW-47-nut-FD-blocker-OOP-early-action-SRP. Per-villain range chains. CO opened 2.5bb: range ~15% (any broadways, pocket pairs 22+, suited connectors, suited aces). On 8s5s2c CO continues with sets (88, 55, 22), spade FDs (Ks-xs, Qs-xs), OESD (76-suited, 64-suited), and pair+draw combos. CO's range remains wide-and-connected on this coordinated board. BTN cold-called the open: range ~8% (suited connectors heavily, pocket pairs 44-JJ, suited broadways). BTN's range is spade-heavy (suited connectors often include spades); many spade FD combos. BB cold-called from BB: very wide range (any defended hand), includes spade FDs broadly. Combined: 3 villains have substantial spade FD equity — the 8s5s board with two spades gives many hands 9-outs to flush. Hero's AsJd: As is the nut spade blocker — reduces the number of nut flush combos across all villain ranges. J overcard provides additional equity (6 outs to top pair if Q-K-A-J don't hit above an 8). Equity realization: 4-way, hero OOP, factor ~0.75 adjusted for early-action pressure from 3 villains behind. Hero is SB, acting first; donk-lead OOP is questionable unless hero has a protection-and-denial argument. Spot-specific factors: The nut-FD blocker (As) is the critical dimension — hero's donk-lead charges villain spade FDs (they must pay to continue drawing). The 8s5s2c board is maximally favorable for villain FD combos; without a bet, spade FDs realize free turns. OOP-early position + 3 villains means pressure exists, but the As blocker plus J overcard gives hero a polarized semi-bluff range that benefits from a small protective c-lead. Decision: BET 25%. Small size leverages the nut-blocker's denial of cheap turns to flush draws + retains pot-control for hero's marginal hand. CHECK risks free turns that complete spade FDs damaging hero's equity trajectory. Alternative large bet (66%) over-commits with a hand that is currently drawing.

Spot 4WF-CLOSING--272: facing_bet=0, hero UTG, Ts9c, turn board 9d4s2cQh (UTG opened preflop, flop checked through 4-way — UTG checked the flop), now turn Q arrives. Bucket: UTG-mid-pair-Q-turn-MW-OOP-check-control. Per-villain range chains. MP cold-called UTG's open: range ~8% (suited connectors, pocket pairs 55-JJ, suited broadways). Flop check-through means MP has medium-strength hands (pairs, weak-draws that didn't want to lead) or air. Q turn: MP's QQ-suited, KQs, AQ all pick up top-pair-or-set. CO cold-called: range similar to MP (~7%), spade draws possible on 4s on flop. Q turn gives CO Q-x value as well. BTN cold-called: closing with suited connectors and pocket pairs; BTN also has Q-x in range (KQ, QJ-suited). Combined: Q turn significantly improves all three villains' ranges — top-pair-Q is now live for any villain who had a Q-x combination in their flatting range. Hero's Ts9c: mid-pair (pair of 9s with T kicker) on a 9d4s2c-Qh board. Hero was the UTG aggressor who checked the flop — this capping action is visible to all villains. Now hero has a 9-pair that is crushed by any Q-x. Equity realization: 4-way still, factor ~0.75, hero OOP and early-action. Spot-specific factors: UTG checked flop (capped range signal); now leading the turn with 9-pair after a Q arrives into three villain ranges that were previously flat-and-waiting is a dominated line. Hero is OOP-early, all three villains apply pressure behind. Donk-lead on Q turn with 9-pair announces weakness (bluff-catching posture) OR Q-x-that-slowplayed, but hero has neither — 9-pair is a pure showdown hand. A bet is both thin (Q-x crushed) and invites exploitation from villain Q-x raising. Decision: CHECK. Preserve SDV by pot-controlling; plan to call a modest bet if one villain bets 25-33%, fold to large aggression. CHECK is clearly dominant here — the hand has SDV vs. non-Q hands that check behind, and loses value vs. any villain with Q-x that raises a donk-lead.

Spot 4WF-MULTIWAY-146: facing_bet=0, hero SB, AsAc, flop Ad2d4c, 4-way SRP, OOP. Bucket: multiway-top-set-FD-board-OOP-protection. Hero has top set (A-A-A on Ad board). Board is Ad2d4c — diamond FD is live (two diamonds already on board; any diamond turn/river = flush possible across 3 villain ranges). Per-villain range chains. CO opened and has range ~15% (pairs 22-AA, suited broadways, suited connectors, off-suit broadways). CO's range on Ad2d4c includes: A-x value (AK, AQ, AJ for top pair; hero has the set-blocker reducing A-x combos for villains), FD hands (K-d-x-d, Q-d-x-d, J-d-x-d, suited connectors in diamonds). CO has many diamond FD combos. BTN cold-called: range ~9% (suited connectors with diamond potential, pocket pairs 33/44 for set potential — 33 = set of 3s possible, 44 = set of 4s possible). Both 33 and 44 in BTN's range give a second or third set on board. BB cold-called: very wide range; A-x in range (A-2o, A-4o, A-5-suited, etc. all pairs with board). BB has strongest probability of two-pair combos (A-2, A-4). Equity realization: 4-way, hero OOP, factor ~0.75. Hero is SB OOP-early, 3 villains behind. Spot-specific factors: top set on FD board in 4-way OOP is the canonical protection-must-bet spot. Each diamond on the turn/river costs hero EV as villains' FD equity realizes cheaply. Hero also blocks A-x combos (holding both aces), reducing villain top-pair range, which makes the bet more credible as value+protection rather than thin. Slow-play loses to free-card completes across 3 villain drawing ranges — combined FD + low-pair-draw equity in 3 villains is substantial. Decision: BET 66% for maximum value and protection. Large sizing charges all FD combos (who have 9 outs per villain, ~37% by river) + two-pair-draws (A-2, A-4) + second-set combos. CHECK-then-CR line is possible but risks two diamonds coming on turn + river with no bet paid on flop. BET 66% is the clearly dominant line.

Spot 4WF-RANGE-AS-436: facing_bet=0, hero BTN, As4s, flop Td8c5s, 3-bet pot HU vs UTG (BTN 3-bet, UTG called), hero IP. This is a direct variant of calibration anchor 4WC-ASYMMETRY-5 (A4s on T-8-5 with same positional setup). Bucket: 3-bet-pot-IP-HU-small-cbet-bluff-backdoor-FD. Per-villain range chains: UTG opened 2.5bb and called a BTN 3-bet to 9bb. UTG's range post-call is range-capped: AA/KK/QQ would typically 4-bet or fold to an IP 3-bet (most UTG regulars 4-bet AA/KK vs BTN squeeze), so UTG's calling range is JJ-TT, AQs, KQs, suited connectors, and sometimes QQ-99 mixing call/4-bet. On Td8c5s: UTG has set potential (TT — set of tens is the big value hand), two-pair candidates (T-8, T-5, 8-5), OESD (76-suited, 97-suited), and overcards AQ/AK that whiffed. UTG's range is medium-connected; contains significant equity but is not heavily nutted. Hero BTN is IP with one opponent. Hero's As4s: backdoor spade nut-FD (one spade on board — 5s — plus As4s gives hero nut flush draw if two more spades come), gutshot OESD (6 for A-2-3-4-5 wheel or 3 for A-2-3-4-5 — actually 4s and As with 5s on board gives 2-3 for wheel). More precisely: A-4 on T-8-5 has A overcard + back-door flush in spades. Equity realization: HU, factor ~1.0. Hero is IP, closing action. Spot-specific factors: BTN is the 3-bettor with range advantage (QQ+/AK/AQ in 3-bet range) and IP position. UTG's capped range has fold equity vs. small c-bets — hands like AQ/KQ with no pair will fold to 25% pot. As is also the spade blocker (reduces villain nut spade combos). Decision: BET 25%. Small c-bet maximizes fold equity against UTG's air (AQ/KQ type) + retains pot control with a marginal hand. Large bets vs. UTG's value (TT set, T-x) bloat the pot with a bluff-equity hand that prefers small sizing. CHECK sacrifices fold-equity and cedes initiative to UTG, who can fire back on dangerous turns. BET 25% is the GTO-consistent line for this 3-bet-pot IP bluff-with-equity situation.

Spot 4WF-4-WAY-3--096: facing_bet=0, hero CO, JdJs, flop QhTs2c, 3-way at decision (BTN is 3-bettor, HJ also cold-called). Hero is cold-caller in a BTN 3-bet pot on Q-T-2 board, OOP relative to BTN. BTN 3-bet to 11bb (with UTG and HJ in the pot, then UTG folded, HJ called, hero called): BTN's 3-bet range is strong but not ultra-premium (QQ+/AK would fold or 4-bet from BTN; BTN 3-bet for value/semi-squeeze includes JJ-QQ, AK, AQ, sometimes KQ-suited, A5s-A2s bluffs). On QhTs2c: BTN c-bet frequency is high — QQ = top set, KK = overpair, AK = two overcards + gutshot (K-J for broadway), JJ = underpair (same as hero). BTN's most dangerous combos: QQ (set), KK (overpair), and AK/KQs (strong equity). BTN is IP-closing: has every reason to c-bet a range-advantage board like Q-T-2. HJ cold-called BTN's 3-bet (HJ had already called UTG open; then called BTN's 3-bet = double-cold-call): HJ's range is extremely capped and strong (QQ-99 that wouldn't 4-bet BTN, AQs, KQs, suited connectors with good equity). HJ has Q-x and T-x combos that connect here. HJ acts before BTN, so HJ is also OOP-early. Hero's JdJs: underpair to Q; top card is Q. JJ loses to Q-x (any Q in villain's ranges), KK, AA. JJ beats T-x, 2-x, underpairs (88-55). Equity realization: 3-way still, factor ~0.85, hero OOP-middle (HJ acts first; hero acts after HJ but before BTN). Spot-specific factors: hero is OOP in a 3-bet pot with an underpair to the board's top card. Donk-lead with JJ on Q-high board is a dominated line — hero's range has no clean value-lead, and BTN (the aggressor) will c-bet the range-advantage board frequently. CHECK preserves optionality: hero can call one c-bet from BTN to realize JJ's SDV (beats T-x, 2-x, and some air), or fold to a large sizing that implies Q-x value. Leading out removes the check-raise line against BTN's air and signals weakness. Decision: CHECK. Hero's JJ has defensive showdown value best realized by checking; the pot-cascade has narrowed to 3-way but BTN's range-advantage on Q-high makes leading an unprofitable donk-lead pattern. Adjacent alternative: BET 25% is possible as a range-balancing lead from a cold-caller, but the underpair-vs-Q tension makes CHECK the cleaner GTO line here.

Spot 4WF-4-WAY-SR-636: facing_bet=0, hero SB, 5d5s, flop Qs9h5c, 4-way SRP, OOP (SB). Hero has bottom set (set of 5s on Q-9-5). Bucket: set-SB-MW-OOP-flop-protection-bet. Per-villain range chains. CO opened 2.5bb: range ~15% (pocket pairs, suited broadways, suited connectors, AK-AJ). On Qs9h5c: CO has Q-x value (AQ, KQ, QJ-suited), set combos (QQ, 99, 55 — but hero holds both 5s, reducing 55 combos for villains), OESD hands (JTs, T8s), FD-hybrid hands (spade draws minimal here — 9h and 5c are not spades; no spade FD on this board). CO connects via top pair and overcards. BTN cold-called: range ~9% (suited connectors 87s/76s/JTs, pocket pairs 66-JJ, suited aces). BTN's range on Qs9h5c includes set-9 (99), OESD (JT-suited, T8-suited), and 2-pair potential (Q-9 combos). BB cold-called from BB: very wide range including Q-x (KQ, QJ, Q-T), 9-x (A9, K9, 98-suited), and two-pair draws (9-5). Hero's 5d5s = bottom set on this board. Equity realization: 4-way, hero OOP-early, factor ~0.75, but set equity is strong enough to override early-action caution. Spot-specific factors: hero has the best made hand possible (bottom set) but bottom set on Q-9-5 is vulnerable — overcards Q and 9 both pair villain ranges heavily, and any J-T-8 run-out creates OESD completions that hurt hero's relative strength. Hero OOP with 3 villains behind means free turn cards are extremely costly (straight draws complete; Q-x two-pairs extend). Bottom set must bet to charge the entire field. Decision: BET 66%. Large sizing for maximum protection + value extraction. Q-x top pair (many combos across CO/BB/BTN) will call for one or two streets at this sizing. OESD hands (JTs, T8s) must call with ~32% equity on flop — charging them is profitable. CHECK hands control away from hero (CO is the preflop aggressor; CO c-bets Q-9-5 for value as the opener). By leading OOP with bottom set, hero charges villain draws while building a pot for turn leverage. Alternative BET 25% charges less and gives drawing hands favorable calls — but at 66%, draws pay negative EV to continue.

Spot-specific factors: this is directly analogous to calibration 4WC-MW45-1 (MW-45 broadway turn completion). Donk-lead with TT on Q turn is dominated: announces a hand that doesn't improve with Q, invites raises from Q-x value across all three villains. Decision: CHECK. TT has SDV against villain non-Q hands (pair of 8s, pocket pairs below TT, 5-x bluff-catchers) but is dominated by the Q-x hands now live in villain ranges. CHECK preserves optionality: hero can call one bet from a single villain but fold to multiway aggression that signals strong Q-x. Spot 4WF-CLOSING--295: facing_bet=0, hero SB, KsKd, flop 7h6s2s, 4-way SRP, OOP (SB). KK = overpair to the board. Two spades on board (6s, 2s) create FD potential. BB cold-called from BB: very wide; any spade-holding hand (Ks-xs, Qs-xs, A-spade combos), 7-x, 6-x, suited connectors for two-pair/OESD. BB's wide range means many spade FD combos land there. Hero's KsKd: Ks is the king of spades — hero holds one of the top spade FD blockers (reduces combo of Ks-xs nut flush draws across villain ranges). Spot-specific factors: hero is SB (OOP-early), all 3 villains apply pressure behind. KK on a 7-6-2 two-tone spade board is a protection-must-bet spot — free turn cards will be devastating: any 8/5/4/3 completes OESD; any spade completes FD. Decision: BET 66%. Large sizing charges all FD combos (9 outs each, ~37% by river) + OESD (8 outs, ~31%) across 3 villain ranges. The Ks blocker in hero's KK reduces the number of nut-spade FD combos, making hero's bet more credible. CHECK-to-induce exposes KK to free turn cards across a board that benefits many villain combos simultaneously. Alternative BET 25% undercharges draws and allows many FD+OESD combos to call profitably; 66% is the correct protection sizing.
